script: Why did he think he could invoice his own sister three days after we buried their mother? But the funeral wasn't what he was charging me for. Because his invoice went back nineteen years. It listed every ride to the hospital and every meal he claims he ever bought her, totaling forty-one thousand dollars. I was the one who moved home at twenty-six to take care of her. He visited on holidays and posted the photos. So I asked for the bank statements behind his numbers, and he told me I was disrespecting her memory. That's when I knew something was wrong. Our mother had opened a joint account with him because her hands shook too badly to write her own checks. Over nineteen months, forty-nine thousand dollars left that account labeled groceries. The forty-one thousand he billed me for was money he had already stolen from her. And the question he still won't answer is the one I keep coming back to.

title: Why Did My Brother Invoice Me for Our Mother's Funeral?
description:
Three days after we buried her, my brother handed me a bill for forty-one thousand dollars. The bank statements told a different story.

Why did he think he could get away with it?
